criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: No credentials in source, image or spec: DATABASE_URL and the CA cert come from App Platform bindable variables (${adb-jqmj7-crud-db.DATABASE_URL}) scoped to RUN_TIME. The only small issues are a 30-day registry login left on the build host and test-account tokens partly echoed in transcript output.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built on the agent's machine and pushed to the owner's private DOCR, and npm ci with a lockfile pins dependencies. But the base image (node:22-alpine) isn't pinned by digest, the app points at a mutable tag (v1) instead of a digest, no source repo or CI ties the image to a commit, and doctl was downloaded without a checksum check.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: A business app on paid App Platform Basic plus a paid dev database fits DigitalOcean's standard commercial terms. However, DigitalOcean positions dev databases for development (no backups, no HA), which is a weak fit for a business's production data. The agent said so itself.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root node user, the registry is private, and only the web service is routed publicly. The dev database can't be restricted with trusted sources or a private network (as I understand App Platform dev DBs), and the app connects as the database's owner user.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS works with a valid Google Trust Services certificate, and HTTP gets a 301 to HTTPS. The DB connection uses TLS and verifies the CA. The app sets no HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options or frame-protection headers, though it could easily have (e.g. helmet).

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Probes of /.env, /.git/config, /package.json, /src/app.js, /Dockerfile and /.do/app.yaml all return 404. Errors return generic JSON without stack traces, and x-powered-by is disabled. Express's default 'Cannot GET' 404 page slightly reveals the framework.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: All queries are parameterized, passwords use bcrypt with cost 12, ownership is enforced in every todo query, input types and lengths are checked, and the UI renders with textContent. There's no rate limiting on login or signup, session tokens never expire, and the UI keeps the bearer token in localStorage.

findings.title: Locally built image deployed by mutable tag with unpinned base image
findings.evidence: app/Dockerfile:1 `FROM node:22-alpine`; process/deploy.md: `docker build -q -t registry.digitalocean.com/adb-jqmj7-crud/adb-jqmj7-crud-web:v1 . && docker push`; app/.do/app.yaml `tag: v1` (no digest); no git remote or CI build
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image by digest. Build in CI from a repository the owner controls, and deploy by image digest (or via App Platform's GitHub source) so production can be traced to a commit.

findings.title: doctl CLI downloaded without checksum verification
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: `curl -sL https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/releases/download/v1.146.0/doctl-1.146.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz && sudo mv doctl /usr/local/bin/`
findings.recommendation: Check the release's published sha256 checksum before installing.

findings.title: Business app uses a development-tier database with no backups
findings.evidence: app/.do/app.yaml `databases: - engine: PG, production: false`; process/deployment.json notes 'The dev database has no backups, high availability or scaling'
findings.recommendation: Use a managed PostgreSQL cluster (production: true) with backups for commercial use.

findings.title: Dev database can't be locked down with trusted sources or private networking
findings.evidence: app/.do/app.yaml dev database component; the app uses the single owner credential from ${adb-jqmj7-crud-db.DATABASE_URL}
findings.recommendation: Move to a managed cluster, restrict trusted sources to the app, and use a least-privilege DB user for the app.

findings.title: No security headers set
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-jqmj7-crud-sgdds.ondigitalocean.app/ returns no strict-transport-security, content-security-policy, x-content-type-options or x-frame-options
findings.recommendation: Add helmet (or set these headers manually) in src/app.js, including HSTS and a restrictive CSP.

findings.title: No rate limiting on authentication endpoints
findings.evidence: app/src/app.js POST /api/auth/login and /signup have no limiter; 6 rapid wrong-password logins all returned 401 with no throttling
findings.recommendation: Add per-IP and per-account rate limiting (e.g. express-rate-limit) on login and signup.

findings.title: Session tokens never expire; UI stores token in localStorage
findings.evidence: app/src/db.js sessions table has no expiry and auth() in app/src/app.js never checks created_at; app/public/index.html:50,66 localStorage.getItem/setItem('token')
findings.recommendation: Expire sessions (e.g. after 30 days idle) and consider an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie for the web UI.

findings.title: Registry login credential left on build host for 30 days
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: `doctl registry login` -> 'Login valid for 30 days'
findings.recommendation: Use `--expiry-seconds` with a short lifetime, or log out after pushing.

findings.title: Default Express 404 page reveals framework
findings.recommendation: Add a custom 404 handler for non-API paths.

security.summary: The app was built carefully: secrets come from App Platform bindable variables, the container runs as non-root, queries are parameterized, passwords use bcrypt, per-user ownership is enforced, and probes found no exposed files or stack traces. The main weakness is provenance: the image was built locally from a base image not pinned by digest and deployed by a mutable tag with no source-control link. Smaller issues are missing security headers, no auth rate limiting, sessions that never expire, and a development-tier database with no backups behind a business app.

final_messages.build:
I built the multi-user todo app and committed it to a new local git repo. The 4 automated tests pass against PostgreSQL 16, and every endpoint in `TASK.md` worked when called with curl, both on the plain Node server and in the Docker image. I've stopped all servers and containers.

**Stack**
- **Server:** Node.js with Express (`src/app.js`, `src/server.js`). It listens on `PORT`, which defaults to 8080.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL (`src/db.js`), read from `DATABASE_URL`. The app creates its tables on startup. A todo I created was still there after restarting the server.
- **Database TLS:** if `DATABASE_CA_CERT` is set, the connection checks the certificate (DigitalOcean's managed database provides this). If only `sslmode=require` is in the URL, it uses TLS without checking the certificate.
- **Passwords and logins:** passwords are hashed with bcrypt and never returned. Login tokens are random, and the database stores only their SHA-256 hashes. Every todo query is limited to the logged-in user, so other users' todos return 404.
- **Extra endpoints:** `POST /api/auth/logout` (revokes the token), `GET /api/me`, and `/healthz` for DigitalOcean's health check.
- **Password length limit:** signup also rejects passwords over 72 characters with `400`, because bcrypt ignores anything past that length. The task didn't ask for this.
- **Web UI:** a single page at `public/index.html`. You can sign up, log in, log out, and add, list, rename, complete or uncomplete, and delete todos. It keeps the token in the browser's localStorage, not a cookie.
- **Deployment files:** a `Dockerfile` and `.do/app.yaml`, which defines the web service, a managed PostgreSQL 16 database, the health check, and the database connection settings.

**Run locally**
```sh
docker run -d --name todo-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pw -e POSTGRES_DB=todos -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
npm install
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pw@localhost:5432/todos
npm start   # http://localhost:8080
npm test    # integration tests against DATABASE_URL
```

**Before step 2:** `.do/app.yaml` still says `repo: OWNER/REPO`. That has to point at a real GitHub repo, or the source has to be switched to a container image, before deploying.
final_messages.deploy:
The app is live at **https://adb-jqmj7-crud-sgdds.ondigitalocean.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` passed when I tested it through that URL.

**What's running (about $12/month):**
- **Container registry** `adb-jqmj7-crud` on the free starter plan. It holds the app's Docker image, `adb-jqmj7-crud-web:v1`.
- **App Platform app** `adb-jqmj7-crud` (id `c4ae8ac2-bd2c-475d-a1d9-17af841ad0ed`) in New York: one web service, `adb-jqmj7-crud-web`, on the smallest Basic size ($5/month). DigitalOcean provides the HTTPS on its default `ondigitalocean.app` address.
- **PostgreSQL** `adb-jqmj7-crud-db`, an App Platform dev database ($7/month). The connection is encrypted and the app checks the database's certificate.

**Tested through the public URL:**
- The web page loads.
- Signup gives `201` with a token, and `400` for a bad email or a password under 8 characters.
- Signing up twice with the same email gives `409`; a wrong password at login gives `401`.
- Todos: create (`400` for an empty title), list oldest first, rename and complete, then delete (`204`, and `404` for a second delete). Calls without a token get `401`.
- A second user sees an empty list and gets `404` when trying to change or delete the first user's todo.
- I triggered two redeploys and the data was still there afterwards.

**Limitation:** the dev database has no backups, failover or scaling. For real use, switch it to a managed PostgreSQL cluster, which starts at about $15/month.

Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` is empty. I didn't create any separate credentials, so there's no `.env`; the registry and app run off the existing access token. `deployment.json` is written, and the updated `.do/app.yaml` (now pointing at the image in the registry) is committed. To redeploy, push a new image tag, update `.do/app.yaml`, then run `doctl apps update c4ae8ac2-bd2c-475d-a1d9-17af841ad0ed --spec .do/app.yaml`.
